title: A whole region disappears
summary: Region A goes dark. Users must keep working, and nothing they wrote may be lost.

statement.situation: Your application serves 4,000 requests/s (about 10% writes — orders and profile changes) from the primary region, Region A. A second region, Region B, exists but has never carried production traffic. At 90 seconds a power event takes Region A completely offline and it does not come back during the incident. The link between regions has an 80 ms round trip.
symptoms: Every request fails until someone repoints traffic
The database in the dead region held the only copy of the most recent writes
When failover finally happens, users report missing orders
requirements: Return to ≥ 99% success within 60 seconds of the outage
Lose no more than 200 acknowledged writes
Keep p99 latency under 500 ms when serving from the surviving region
constraints: Anything in a region goes down with it — place components deliberately
The users' entry point sits outside both regions
Cross-region calls pay the 80 ms round trip

background: Drag components into Region A or Region B. Edges that cross between regions add the round-trip time automatically.
learningObjectives: RPO vs latency: synchronous vs asynchronous replication across regions
Failover detection and client caching delays

references.title: AWS Builders' Library: Static stability using Availability Zones
AWS post-event summary: us-east-1, 19-20 Oct 2025 (DNS effects on recovery)

scenarios.name: Region A is lost at t=90 s
scenarios.description: 4,000 req/s for 6 minutes. Region A goes offline at t=90 s and stays down. Cross-region round trip: 80 ms.

successCriteria.label: ≥ 99% of requests succeed within 60 s of the outage
